title: Persian Period Jerusalem and Yehud: A Rejoinder

verification_log.method: Introduction: Persian-period Jerusalem was "a small settlement" of ca. 2–2.5 ha, "no more than a few hundred people"; a century of archaeology "has failed to reveal any trace of a city-wall" datable to the Persian period and identifiable as Nehemiah's; Neh 3 "may represent the reality" of the Hasmonean First Wall; "Nehemiah's Wall … built on quicksand": E. Mazar's finds under the northern tower in Area G give only a terminus post quem; the most logical date for the tower is late Hellenistic (Hasmonean)

access_notes: Read in full (PDF). Summarises Finkelstein, JSOT 32 (2008) 501–520, which was not read.
